about: Vectors for the x402/exact/casper pairing: the casper entry point of @integraledger/lcp. H is SHA-256("abc") from FIPS 180-2; the option, payee and payer are x402's Casper example; the EIP-712 values were computed with @casper-ecosystem/casper-eip-712 1.2.1 and, separately, viem 2.57.4 over CEP-3009's formula by hand, on Node 26.10.0; every SHA-256 with GNU coreutils sha256sum. The public key and signature are placeholders of the tagged widths: bound verifies no signature. Byte strings are hex; uint256 values are decimal strings; a call's blockHeight is a decimal string. C3's rows change only validBefore: CEP-3009's transfer_with_authorization takes valid_before as a u64 and names u64::MAX the value that never expires, and reference records settleBy as validBefore up to 2^53-1, ECMAScript's Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and as 2^53-1 above it, and refuses a validBefore of 2^64 or more. C4 and C5 read status over constructed nodes, described in C4's about; C5 holds the act agreement.

C2.case: complete(publicKey, signature), then bound. expectPayload is x402 v2's PaymentPayload written by hand from the specifications (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2): its members in the order of specs/x402-specification-v2.md §5.2.1 (x402Version, resource, accepted, payload), and the Casper payload as specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_casper.md L13-17 and its example PaymentPayload L39-50 write it (authorization, then publicKey and signature, the fixed placeholders), the authorization's members in the order of L40-47 with C1.expectMessage's values; Python 3.12.3's json.dumps of that object, compact, is the JSON text of expectPayload.

C4.about: status over a constructed node (no answer of a live node is recorded yet): head, the newest executed block; lowest, its available_block_range.low; setFrom, the first height at which used_nonces[(from, nonce)] of the reference's asset is set (null: unset at every height); pages, the executed transactions of block setFrom, a page each; fail, the reader rejects. nonceUsed answers null below lowest and above head. Heights and amounts are decimal strings; a call's nonce is hex. Each transfer of what moved is named by its transaction and its place, the transaction's own call to the package by its entry point. Each expected answer is derived from the profile's rules 12 to 22 and read-status.md, none taken from the package's output.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.
